doc.title: Wilson "Chembo" Corniel interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, November 15, 2019

title: Making a living as an independent: Chemboro Records and college clinics
summary: He runs Chemboro Records, had a Grammy nomination in 2010, does all business roles himself, and plays college clinics.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Managers, bookers and the business of getting work

blocks.x: So what’s it like to make a living as a musician in New York City. Do you have to wear lots of hats?

Oh yeah, especially for myself, I’m an independent record company, Chemboro Records, I’ve had it since 2004. I have five CDs under my label. The third CD, “Things I Wanted to Do” in 2010 was nominated for a Grammy of Best Latin Jazz by the American Grammy, NARAS. I was nominated along with Chucho Valdes, Miguel Zenon, Claudio Roditi, and Geoff Keezer, pianist I guess. But when you have a name like Chucho Valdes, “Who is Chembo?” “Who is Chembo?” But at least being nominated and being an independent, so I have to wear the hat of being a promoter, I’m my accountant, I’m the band boy, I’m the manager, I’m the booking agent. Then I’ve got to practice. So of course I’m wearing all these hats because I’m independent. I’m not going to go to a manager who has five bands, and he’s going to give the work to his top guys, he’ll give you the crumbs. You know I just pick up the phone and I’ll do all that myself. It’s harder you know, it’s harder because I have to do all that. It’s not like before. Clubs are closing you know, so I have to look for these circuits with the colleges. And I like that I see there was a void in learning our music this way, like I was explaining to you. You know I feel that we — doing these rounds, I just came last week I was at Tufts doing the same thing. I did two clinics and I did a concert with the professor’s Latin jazz band at the school. And I was there with my group last year doing the same thing. So he puts me into his jazz class with his students and we do the same thing, and try to show them a little one-on-one mambo, tumbao, Latin, you know, to be the real style and how to play a clave. The clave is so important because in Latin music, the clave in Spanish music is key. That’s the key
